thread:
Sam: FYI I just saw a replay run from the canary job that included full request bodies. Looks like our replay path rehydrates the original payload before scrubbers run. :eyes:
Maria: ugh. do you have the trace id?
Sam: trace=tr-20260315-88a2, replay job id 20260315-88a2-replay. deploy-bot: replay-job-started id=20260315-88a2-replay user=ci/canary
Maria: got it. root cause: inspect-mode flag is still being honored by the runtime during replay. our scrubber pipeline is gated behind the normal ingress path, but replays currently call internal/rehydrate() which bypasses request middleware.
Rahul: can we change rehydrate to pass through the same scrub pipeline? simpler: always apply deid on any non-prod-replay unless explicit consent is present.
Liz: Agree we should make the safer default. UX question: console currently shows a "replay details" button that toggles full payload. If we mask by default, how do we support breakglass for SREs?
Maria: proposal: add a per-replay metadata field consent_token and a console-level breakglass approval workflow. Without approval, UI shows masked values and audit-log entry. With approval, the payload is shown but the action is logged and TTL-limited.
Sam: sounds ok. Implementation notes: two parts - runtime change so rehydrate always routes through scrubber, and console flow for breakglass + audit record. Also need a telemetry event so we can track how often breakglass is used.
Rahul: telemetry: replay.view_unmasked with properties {replay_id, approver, duration_seconds}. Also increment an internal quota counter for unmasked views to limit risk.
Liz: edge-case: what about legal-approved debug for customer support? We need a consent token that can be generated via the admin console scoped to customer and case id. That token should be exchangeable by the runtime with short TTL.
Sam: agree. security caveat: don't put raw token in logs. only store hashed token and store who requested it.
Maria: config snippet for runtime patch (pseudo):
```
# runtime config fragment
replay:
  scrub_through_middleware: true
  allow_unmasked_if: 
    - has_valid_consent_token
    - requester_role in [sre,admin]
```
Sam: QA plan: canary patch to runtime (1.2.3-canary-replay-scrub) -> run replay job on staging traces -> verify masked by default + breakglass audit -> ship to prod.
Rahul: timeline? I can do the runtime change today, Maria can wire the audit event, Liz can prototype console modal.
Maria: I’ll add the telemetry patch and a data dog dashboard for replay.unmasked_count and replay.mask_failure_rate.
Sam: ok owners: Rahul(runtime), Maria(telemetry+audit), Liz(console breakglass). Rahul: please open PR and tag @maria @liz. :thumbsup:
Rahul: will do. PR coming in ~2h.
deploy-bot: replay-job-completed id=20260315-88a2-replay status=completed scrub_status=failed (no consent token)
Sam: thanks — good catch. we have a short-term mitigation: disable replay-unmasked in CI canaries until runtime patch lands.
Liz: i'll add a console flag to block unmasked replays from CI users.
Sam: perfect. tracking ticket in board: PLAT-1429 (add runtime scrub for replays + breakglass).
